 B.Sudheendra Kumar, J.

The first accused in C.C. No.33 of 2002 on the files of the Judicial Magistrate of First Class - III,
Thrissur filed this revision petition challenging the judgment of the appellate court remanding the matter to the trial court for the purpose of granting an opportunity to the revision petitioner to adduce evidence to avail the benefit under Section 19(2) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act,
1954 (for short 'the PFAAct').
2.

entities.text: Judicial Magistrate of First Class - III
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Heard.

3. The prosecution allegation can be briefly stated thus:-
On 10.10.2001, PW1, the Food Inspector, purchased four sealed packets of tea dust from the first accused.
The second accused was the distributor of the said item.
After sampling as per rules, one of the samples was sent for analysis to the Public Analyst.
The Public Analyst filed Ext. P22 report stating that the sample did not conform to the standard prescribed for the food item and was, therefore adulterated.

It was further reported in Ext.P22 report that the sample contained added synthetic colours,
namely, tartrazine, sunset yellow food colour and carmoisine and therefore, it was adulterated.
4. Before the trial Court, PW1 to PW4 were examined and Exts. P1 to P36 series were marked for the prosecution.
DW1 was examined and Ext.D1 was marked on the side of the revision petitioner.

5. The trial court, after evaluating the evidence, found the revision petitioner guilty under Sections 16(1A)(i), 2 (ia)(j) and 7(i)(v) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 read with Rule 5 Appendix B, A.14 and rule 29 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955, convicted and sentenced him thereunder.

In the appeal, the conviction and sentence passed by the trial court were set aside and the matter was remanded to the trial court to enable the revision petitioner to adduce evidence to avail the benefit Section 19(2) of the P.F.A. Act.

6. When this matter has been taken up for hearing, the learned counsel for the revision petitioner has submitted that in view of the decision of the Apex Court in Pepsico India Holdings (P) Ltd. v.
Food Inspector [(2011) 1 SCC 176], there is no need to remand the matter to adduce evidence for availing the benefit under Section 19(2) of the P.F.A. Act and in the said circumstances, the learned counsel has pleaded for setting aside the judgment of the appellate Court remanding the case to the trial court.

sentences.text: The appellate court remanded the matter to the trial court only for the purpose of giving the appellant an opportunity to adduce evidence, if any, to avail the benefit under Section 19(2) of the PFA Act.

Admittedly, no laboratory was defined and no validated method of analysis was Peter Mathew vs The Food Inspector on 14 March, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/39147206/
2 prescribed as provided under Section 23 (1-A)(ee) and (hh) of the PFA Act.

entities.text: Peter Mathew vs The Food Inspector
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the said circumstances, I am of the view that there is no need to grant opportunity to the revision petitioner to avail the benefit under Section 19(2) of the Act, in view of the decision of the Apex Court in Pepsico India Holdings (P) Ltd.(supra).
For the said reason, the judgment of the appellate court remanding the matter to the trial court cannot be sustained and consequently, I set aside the same.

In the result, this revision petition stands allowed, setting aside the judgment of the appellate court remitting the matter to the court below and the matter is remanded to the appellate court for fresh disposal of the appeal in accordance with law, affording reasonable opportunity to the revision petitioner of being heard.
The revision petitioner shall appear before the appellant court on 28.5.2016 through the counsel without further notice.
